mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals active monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in less than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or correlation between FEDFUNDS decline and SPX return is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate falls below 2.0% in the prior month, it triggers aggressive monetary easing expectations, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through lower borrowing costs.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 45% of instances when FEDFUNDS falls below 2.0%, or average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) signal a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in less than 55% of instances where PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or joint effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL 12-month change exceeding 3.5%), the market prices in aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to rising discount rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in less than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL 12m change exceeds 3.5%, or average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP growth rate (GDPC1) indicates robust economic activity supporting corporate profit growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in less than 55% of instances when GDPC1 rises, or correlation between GDPC1 growth and SPX return is insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0, it signals economic contraction leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to weakening output.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 45% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100.0, or average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) both rise, it indicates strong consumer demand supporting corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in less than 55% of instances where PAYEMS and HOUST both rise, or joint effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, rising housing starts (HOUST) above 1400.0 indicate peak economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates a slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in less than 55% of instances when HOUST exceeds 1400.0, or average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
